source: Bass, Geddes, Wright, Coderre, Rikers, McLaughlin (2013) Experienced physicians benefit from analyzing initial diagnostic hypotheses
finding: Gap 4 primary source. 9 nephrologists and 6 nephrology residents diagnosed 10 cases. They gave an initial diagnosis from presenting features, then were primed to use either hypothetico-deductive or scheme-inductive reasoning on the rest of the case data, then gave a final diagnosis.
numbers: Initial vs final accuracy: nephrologists 31.1% vs 65.6% (p<0.001); residents 40.0% vs 70.0% (p<0.001). Experience x strategy interaction p=0.02. Residents did better with scheme-inductive (OR 5.69, CI 1.59-20.33); nephrologists no difference between strategies (OR 0.57, CI 0.23-1.39).
limits: PubMed abstract page read, not the full paper. There is NO control group that got the extra case data without the priming step, so the gain cannot be credited to analysing the hypothesis; it may simply come from receiving more data. Abstract reports p=0.07 beside an OR whose CI excludes 1, an internal inconsistency. N=15 total. Both strategies were primed, so hypothetico-deductive was not shown to beat free reasoning.
agent_relevance: K09 stays contested. Do not treat 'analyse initial hypothesis' as proven. A fair test needs an arm that sees the same extra data with no hypothesis step.

source: Neufeld, Norman, Feightner, Barrows (1981) Clinical problem-solving by medical students: a cross-sectional and longitudinal analysis
finding: Gap 6, replication of the Elstein finding. Students from three classes (cross-sectional) plus 22 students followed yearly from preclerkship to first postgraduate year, against a doctor criterion group. Most reasoning process variables were unrelated to educational level. Outcomes rose with education. The only process variable tied to both level and outcome was a 'hypothesis aggregate score', a measure of hypothesis content.
numbers: 22 students in the longitudinal arm; stimulated recall of videotaped simulated-patient encounters; four outcome measures. Exact effect sizes not in abstract.
quote: the problem-solving or clinical reasoning process remains relatively constant from medical school entry to practice
limits: Abstract read only. Supports the content-specificity view: the process stays constant from school entry to practice; only content quality changes.
agent_relevance: Strong support for K02 and for Elstein's own pivot: loop structure is not what separates strong from weak. For the agent, put effort into hypothesis content and knowledge, not loop shape.

source: Barrows, Norman, Neufeld, Feightner (1982) The clinical reasoning of randomly selected physicians in general medical practice
finding: Gap 6, independent replication in a different population. 18 family physicians and 19 general internists were randomly selected; 62 encounters with 4 simulated patient problems were studied. Physicians consistently formed multiple diagnostic hypotheses early and used them to guide inquiry, not routine comprehensive data collection. Little variation between problems. Accuracy and promptness of hypothesis generation were linked to accuracy of the diagnostic formulation.
limits: Abstract read only; no counts of hypotheses in abstract. Simulated patients.
agent_relevance: Confirms the descriptive core of K01 (early hypotheses guide search) outside Elstein's lab, and ties speed plus accuracy of the first hypotheses to outcome (supports K18).

source: Feightner, Barrows, Neufeld, Norman (1977) Solving problems: how does the family physician do it?
finding: Early McMaster description of the thought processes of family physicians in clinical problem solving, which led to a model of the process. Abstract gives no figures.
agent_relevance: Historical link only: the McMaster group reached the same hypothesis-guided model independently of Michigan State.

source: Elstein (2009) Thinking about diagnostic thinking: a 30-year perspective
finding: Gap 6. The author of the founding studies says the paper reviews the major findings of Medical Problem Solving and summarises criticisms of the hypothesis-testing model that led to more emphasis on clinical experience and prior knowledge.
quote: criticisms of the hypothesis-testing model ... led to greater emphasis on the role of clinical experience and prior knowledge
limits: Only the abstract was reachable (publisher page needs login). The exact 1978 counts (hypotheses per case, minutes to first hypothesis, accuracy by group) remain unverified from a primary reading.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 exact numbers stay open. They need the 1978 book or this 2009 paper in full.

source: Five decades of research and theorization on clinical reasoning: a critical review (BMC Med Educ 2019)
finding: Full text read via Europe PMC. Describes the hypothetico-deductive model as proposed by Elstein (1978): physicians generate a limited number of diagnostic hypotheses and then test them. Says case-specificity findings challenged the model as an adequate description, and that Elstein defended it as turning an unstructured problem into a structured one.
agent_relevance: The field records the model as kept for problem structuring, dropped as an explanation of expertise.

source: How cognitive psychology changed the face of medical education research (Adv Health Sci Educ 2020)
finding: Full text read via Europe PMC. The hypothetico-deductive method was shown by 1970s think-aloud studies, but later studies (Elstein 1978; Neufeld 1981 cited) showed it does not explain expert performance. Students used the same approach; what separated experts from novices was the quality of hypotheses (Barrows et al.). Elstein named this content specificity.
limits: Secondhand; supports the replication chain d02/d03 but adds no new data.
agent_relevance: Same lesson: reward hypothesis quality and knowledge, not hypothesis count.

source: Sprafka (1973) doctoral dissertation, Michigan State (30 fourth-year students; hypothesis number and timing)
finding: Gap 3 primary source NOT reached. The MSU repository returned an access-limited notice for both candidate records (41739, 41740). Only the earlier search-result summary is available: N=30, instructions to generate many or few hypotheses, early or late, made little difference to outcome; low-accuracy subjects produced more varied inaccurate hypotheses.
limits: Not read. K17 stays single-source and secondhand.
agent_relevance: Open: no human primary evidence on the optimal number of hypotheses. The LLM data in d11 is the only measured curve.

source: Nori et al. (2025) Sequential Diagnosis with Language Models, role and variant design (arXiv 2506.22405 full text)
finding: Gap 2. Full PDF text searched for ablations. MAI-DxO has five roles (Hypothesis, Test-Chooser, Challenger, Stewardship, Checklist) played by one model. The five reported variants (Instant Answer, Question Only, Budgeted, Unconstrained, Ensemble) change questions, tests, budget tracking and ensembling, NOT individual roles. The only ablation run is single-turn vs batched questioning on the 56-case test set.
numbers: Single vs batched mode: both 83.9% accuracy; cost $3,991 (single) vs $5,084 (batch). Budgeted 79.9% at $2,396; ensemble 85.5% at $7,184; o3 baseline $7,850. 304 NEJM cases, 56 held-out test.
limits: Authors say all variants used the same orchestration structure with capabilities selectively enabled or disabled. Role effect is not isolated. No third-party ablation or replication found in sources I could reach (secondary web coverage also reported none).
agent_relevance: Gap 2 stays OPEN. Claims that the Challenger or hypothesis tracker carries the gain are untested. Do not credit S3/S4 hypothesis tracking from Nori; build our own role ablation.

source: Nori et al. (2025) Sequential Diagnosis with Language Models, manual case inspection
finding: Authors manually inspected cases where MAI-DxO (no budget) disagreed with baseline o3. MAI-DxO often sought disconfirming evidence and switched path, while o3 seemed to anchor on first impressions and to order reasonable tests rather than max-information tests.
quote: MAI-DxO often sought disconfirming evidence and switched its diagnostic path
limits: Anecdotal attribution to Dr. Hypothesis and Dr. Challenger by the authors, not measured. Gatekeeper LLM can leak cues.
agent_relevance: A hypothesis to test: a disconfirmation step at equal tokens. Not evidence yet.

source: Wang, Sheng, Li, Qu, Sun, Zhu (2026) MedKGI: iterative differential diagnosis with medical knowledge graphs and information-guided inquiring
finding: Gaps 3, 5, 7. Ablation on agent-MedQA with Qwen3-8B. Removing the knowledge graph (the knowledge source) costs 25.5 points. Replacing information-gain question choice with random node choice drops accuracy to 31.1%. The paper's own hyperparameter study finds accuracy peaks at 5 candidate diseases and declines with more.
numbers: Full 69.81% (9.11 rounds). w/o knowledge graph 44.34% (13.44 rounds). w/o clinical record 57.55%. Random node selection 31.13% (19.25 rounds). Degree-based selection 47.17%. Candidate-count peak at 5 (from text; figure not read).
limits: One 8B open model, one dataset, simulated patients, authors' own system. Knowledge graph confounds knowledge and structure. The 5-candidate peak is for their pipeline only; unknown for frontier models.
agent_relevance: Partial answer to gap 3: an inverted U with a peak near 5 is measured once, matching the classic few hypotheses. Partial answer to gap 7: knowledge matters as much as selection. It contradicts the random-planner win in c14, so gap 5 depends on setup.

source: Ge, Li, Wang, Hu, Zhang, Li (2026) ClinicalAgents: multi-agent orchestration for clinical decision making with dual-memory (KDD 2026)
finding: Gaps 2 and 7. Ablation on MedChain with GPT-5.2 separates memory (knowledge/experience) from an MCTS orchestrator with backtracking over hypotheses. Each part adds about equally; together they add most. The orchestrator reports hypothesis pruning and recovery from a wrong first hypothesis.
numbers: Average score: backbone 0.4521; +dual memory 0.4762 (as read; table columns garbled); +orchestrator 0.4962 (+9.8%); all 0.5107 (+13.0%). When the initial hypothesis was wrong: backtracking triggered in 83%, correct diagnosis recovered in 64%. At least one unsupported hypothesis pruned in 94% of cases.
limits: Average of six metrics across a multi-stage workflow, not diagnosis accuracy alone. Authors' own system; no variance or test; memory-only number least certain. Recovery 64% has no baseline without backtracking.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: knowledge/memory and loop control are each worth about 3-5 points, so neither alone explains it. A small measured case for a revise-on-contradiction step (S4/S5).

source: Ke et al. (2024) Enhancing diagnostic accuracy through multi-agent conversations: LLMs to mitigate cognitive bias
finding: Gap 8. Four GPT-4 agents (diagnoser, devil's advocate against confirmation and anchoring, facilitator against premature closure, recorder) re-examined 16 case reports of bias-caused misdiagnosis, 5 runs each.
numbers: Initial diagnosis 0/80 correct; after discussion top differential 57/80 (71.3%), top two 64/80 (80.0%).
limits: Cases were chosen because the first diagnosis was wrong, so the 0% start is built in and regression to the mean is expected. No equal-token control and no devil's-advocate-removed arm. Published cases may be in training data. Body text says 15 of 162 cases selected in one place, abstract says 16.
agent_relevance: Cannot answer gap 8. Shows an LLM can recover from a known-wrong anchor with extra turns; does not show the disconfirmation role is the cause.

source: Handler, Bedi, Shah (2026) Quantifying and mitigating premature closure in frontier LLMs
finding: Gap 9. Five frontier LLMs committed to an answer when the correct option was removed or the case was underspecified. A short safety-oriented system prompt cut premature closure but not to zero.
numbers: MedQA n=500 and AfriMed-QA n=490 with correct choice removed: baseline false action 55-81% and 53-82% (mean about 70%); with safety prompt about 48% on both; Gemini 2.5 Pro 55% to 48%. HealthBench 861 questions: inappropriate answers 30% average; 78% of 191 physician adversarial queries. Underspecified low-risk cases 73-96% premature closure (mean 81%) vs urgent cases 5-36% (mean 19%). Excluding Grok 3, accuracy on answerable items fell 1.0 point on average.
limits: Prompt-only intervention; different task from sequential diagnosis; Grok 3 over-corrected (accuracy loss).
agent_relevance: Gap 9, partial: models do not reliably detect when information is insufficient; they escalate when stakes are visible and commit when the case looks routine. A stop/ask gate based on self-detected difficulty is weak. Supports an abstain guard in the schema.

source: Chiu, Pitis, van der Schaar (2025) Simulating viva voce examinations to evaluate clinical reasoning in LLMs (VivaBench)
finding: Gaps 1, 5, 9. 1,152 vignettes run as multi-turn exams. All six models did far worse when they had to gather data than when given full information. LLM-classified failures were mostly reasoning (hypothesis generation, early closure), not knowledge.
numbers: Appendix approximate top-1: provisional / final / full-information: Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.65 / 0.75 / 0.93; DeepSeek-R1 0.61 / 0.71 / 0.93; Llama-4 0.59 / 0.70 / 0.91; Grok 3 Mini 0.61 / 0.65 / 0.92. Main-text exact top-1: Gemini final 35% vs full information 69%. Failure counts: inappropriate hypothesis generation 348 cases, premature closure 291, inadequate investigation 90, ICD coding 9. Confidence rose on maintained diagnoses whether or not correct.
limits: Appendix approximate and main-text exact accuracy use different matching; do not mix scales. Failure classification by an LLM (text leaves a count as X). No scaffold arm, so no test of whether a hypothesis step helps.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: knowledge is present (about 0.93 with full data); loss comes from the gather-and-revise loop. Argues for work on S4/S5 but gives no scaffold comparison.

source: Cao and Chen (2026) VeriDx: disease-centric verification of diagnostic reasoning
finding: Gap 10, indirect. An evaluation framework that checks whether each hypothesis a model proposes has its obligations met (key evidence checked, alternatives excluded, contradictions resolved, closure justified). Its ablation of checker modules shows removing disease profiles lowers scores most.
numbers: Ablation rows seen: w/o profiles 0.80/0.36/0.33/0.62/0.79/0.48; w/o phenotype 0.85/0.61/0.59/0.64/0.82/0.61; w/o closure 0.87/0.50/0.46/0.65/0.82/0.60 (column names not verified).
limits: Measures audit quality, not whether a final-answer verification step raises diagnostic accuracy. Only intro and ablation table read.
agent_relevance: Does NOT close gap 10. Possible checker design (hypothesis obligations) for a later experiment.
